segments.title: Make the experience universal
segments.narration: If Arabic is unfamiliar, you just felt the gap between hearing words and following their meaning. About two billion people are Muslim, roughly one quarter of the world’s population. For many of us, that gap is part of everyday listening. What if meaning could stay with us?
segments.visual: One hundred marks arrive, twenty-five turn red, and the marks regroup into four equal groups. About 2 billion and about one quarter land beside the dated Pew source caption.
segments.overlay:
About 2 billion Muslims · about one quarter of the world’s population
Pew Research Center · 2020 estimate, published 2025 · underlying share 25.6%

segments.title: Name the product and Meta stack
segments.narration: Meet Ayah Lens. Meta glasses, Muse Voice, and Muse Spark, working together to bring Quran recitation and its English meaning into view.
segments.visual: Original animated 3D geometry approximates the black Meta Ray-Ban Display. A changing perspective and moving light accompany staggered stack names. Label 3D illustration; the lenses contain no invented output.
segments.overlay:
Ayah Lens
Meta glasses + Muse Voice + Muse Spark

segments.title: Carry one listening experience between settings
segments.narration: During Salat, Muslim prayer, it could help listeners follow the recitation. At home, it can follow a reciter playing on television. Hands free.
segments.visual: Prayer and home listening settings share travelling explanatory sound envelopes and a traced rule. The prayer disclaimer stays readable.
segments.overlay: Technology demonstration only. This does not establish religious permissibility for use during prayer.

segments.title: Reveal the difficult part hiding in plain sight
segments.narration: Now look closer. We are still inside the same passage. A long verse cannot fit on this lens. Ayah Lens follows the recitation through it, showing the relevant portion as the words continue. Nobody is turning a page.
segments.visual: An explanatory highlighted source window advances over abstract word positions. The genuine 73:20 phone source card keeps changing on the right, with no change to its wording or playback speed.
segments.overlay:
Same passage · changing portions
No manual paging

segments.title: Explain the actual AI and tracking work
segments.narration: Muse Voice converts the glasses’ audio into Arabic text. Muse Spark helps pair Arabic phrases with portions of a published English translation. It can also assist with uncertain passage matches. Our software tracks the position, validates the source boundaries, and sends the current portion to the glasses.
segments.visual: Animated data moves from glasses audio through Muse Voice transcription, local canonical matching and portion tracking, published Arabic/Pickthall source, and the lens window. Spark branches only when needed for bounded ambiguity and validated cached paired-source plans.
segments.overlay:
Muse Voice · live transcription
Muse Spark · source pairing and ambiguity assistance
Filmed phrase plans cached

segments.title: Show memorization practice and listener choice
segments.narration: Hifz means memorizing the Quran. Arabic-only mode offers a reference while rehearsing. Turn English back on whenever you want to follow the meaning.
segments.visual: A labelled Hifz reference schematic gains published English meaning as an explanatory mode change. This graphic is not filmed switch proof or a tajweed grader.

segments.title: Establish the working foundation
segments.narration: The reference covers all 114 surahs. We built the glasses integration and automatic following during this hackathon. Fifty-nine tests cover matching, source preservation, and display scheduling. With further development and extensive testing, future versions could support Quran teaching.
segments.visual: The 114-surah, 6,236-reference-ayah and 59-test figures build separately. A yellow future-teaching insert states that further development and extensive testing are required.
